messages:
Avery: FYI product wants to flip OrchID-13B live next Tue. Early bench shows ~2.5x token/sec per request vs our current baseline. Need a quick capacity + cost projection and a safe rollout plan.

Kai: Do we have the recent baseline numbers (tokens/sec, GPU-hrs/day, regional split) to compare against?

Maya: Baseline (7d avg):
- agg tokens/sec: 420,000
- avg seq len: 150
- active A100-eq GPUs: 120
- avg GPU-hrs/day: 2400
- peak 5m tokens/sec: 680,000

Quick rough projection if OrchID drives 2.5x token/sec:
- projected tokens/sec ~1,050,000
- naive GPU-hrs scale -> ~2400 * 2.5 = 6000 GPU-hrs/day
Note: this linear estimate ignores KV-cache pressure and larger per-token decoder cost.

Ravi: Regional capacity constraints: US-W has room for +40 GPUs fast, EU-W can add ~10 immediately but procurement lead time for big blocks is weeks, APAC is full. Also EU-W egress sits around 80Gbps at peaks; OrchID responses trend longer, might push us past saturation.

Kai: Mitigation ideas:
- Canary 10% traffic in US-W for 48h (health hooks + trace sampling)
- Expose quantized (8-bit) variant for hosted dev tier where quality tolerates it
- Reduce max_tokens for free/guest tiers temporarily
- Aggressive prefix caching for commonly repeated prompts
- Short-term burst capacity via spot + reserved mix from partners

Maya: Microbench results: OrchID-13B with our kernel set decodes ~1.6x slower per token than our 7B baseline under same batching. Also KV-cache pressure adds ~20% overhead for long sequences. Realistic GPU-hrs/day therefore likely in the 6500-7200 range until we tune batching/quant.

Avery: Cost ballpark: assume $2.80/GPU-hr avg blended infra price -> at 7000 GPU-hrs/day that's ~$19.6k/day incremental (~$588k/mo if sustained). Product needs to confirm target qps and expected ramp window.

Ravi: Procurement note: large dedicated reservations in EU-W take ~4-6 weeks. US-W shorter via cloud partners; I'll start a ticket for a 3-month temporary block in US-W and a smaller one in EU-W.

Kai: Proposed rollout plan (draft):
1) Canary 10% in US-W for 48h with SLO monitors and tail-latency alerts
2) If stable, scale to 30% with autoscale policy temp bump + burst pool
3) Roll out 8-bit quant to >=developer paid tiers for ~30% of traffic to cut token-cost
4) Throttle or cap non-paid tiers if cost/exposure crosses threshold

Maya: I'll publish a short forecast sheet by EOD with region rows: GPU-hrs, network egress, and cost under two scenarios: Optimistic (batching +30% efficiency) and Conservative (no batching gains).

Ravi: Procurement ticket PR-4728 opened and assigned to @Lena. ETA approval 48-72h. Also pinged partners for temporary APAC capacity.

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary job: job/orchid-canary-1760044800 queued by Kai

Kai: I'll also add an autoscaler cooldown tweak and a new circuit-breaker rule: reject >5k concurrent requests per-model-per-region to avoid cascading.

Avery: Product wants a go/no-go by 09:00 Monday. Can we get the forecast + canary runbook in the thread? :thumbsup: 

Maya: Draft sheet uploaded: https://redwood.internal/sheets/orchid-capacity-proj (draft). Runbook (short):
- Canary config: 10% traffic, 48h, sample traces 1%
- Monitors: 95/99/999 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, network egress by AZ
- Rollback: automated fallback to baseline model on >3 consecutive 5m SLO breaches

Lena: Procurement acked PR-4728 and requested expected utilization curve + burn-rate. I'll attach Maya's forecast.

Avery: Good. If anyone hits blockers spinning up US-W capacity, ping me immediately.

Kai: Noted. Will post canary job link once it starts and add runbook to #eng-runtime/resources.

Maya: Done 1: will iterate the sheet after canary results.

Avery: Thanks team.
